title: Religion
tagline: Oracle bones, sutras, Daoist scriptures, Shinto rites, shamans and new religions from the Shang to the twentieth century
hero_file: Diamond Sutra of 868 AD - The Diamond Sutra (868), frontispiece and text - BL Or. 8210-P.2.jpg
hero_caption: Frontispiece of the Diamond Sutra printed in 868, found in the Library Cave at Dunhuang (British Library, Or. 8210/P.2)
intro: The religious life of China, Japan and Korea: Shang divination and ancestor cults, Confucian ritual, religious Daoism, the many schools of East Asian Buddhism, Shinto, Korean shamanism, popular religion, the arrival of Christianity and the new religions of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. In East Asia these traditions were rarely exclusive; most people drew on several at once, and this section treats them as overlapping strands of one religious landscape. It is written as history of religion, describing what each tradition teaches and practises and what modern scholarship says about authorship and dating, without taking sides. Manuscripts, early prints, temple paintings and portrait sculptures come from Wikimedia Commons.
